1 ONLY IN SO FAR AS DISCHARGING ACCUSED NO.2.
 THIS CRIMINAL PETITION COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The State has filed this petition challenging the order passed by the learned Sessions Judge confirming the order passed by the learned Magistrate discharging accused No.2 for the offences under Sections 498A and 506 of IPC read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. Heard the learned High Court Government Pleader for the State and learned counsel for respondent.
3.
Accused No.1/Husband and Accused No.2/mother-in-law of the defacto complainant filed an application for discharging under Section 239 Cr.P.C.
The learned Magistrate allowed the application and discharged the accused for the aforesaid offence, against which the State filed the Revision Petition before the learned Sessions Judge.

The learned Sessions Judge after perusing the material on record, dismissed the Revision Petition as against accused No.2 stating that there are no specific allegations of demand of money insofar as accused No.2/mother-in-law of the defacto complainant.

4. The findings recorded by the learned Magistrate as well as the learned Sessions Judge is based on the charge sheet material, and in the absence of any arbitrary or perversity in recording the said findings, the impugned order passed by the learned Sessions Judge cannot be faulted with.
5. I do not find any good ground to interfere in the well reasoned order passed by the Trial Court and the Revision Court.
